answers.question: Should write-back locate the target node and splice only its replacement text into the original file (A), use a ruamel.yaml round-trip dump (B), or something else (C)?
answers.reply: A. The contract requires byte-surgical write-back: after a successful `set`, the only bytes that differ in any file are the ones the `set` section requires to change. Users hand-edit these files and review the diffs, so byte-surgical write-back matters more than speed. You may pick any technique that guarantees this. A round-trip dump that normalises indentation, quoting, flow spacing, folded scalars or comment spacing would break that rule.
answers.cited: Contract: set PATH VALUE (byte-surgical write-back rule); Brief: Standing answers (users hand-edit and review diffs; byte-surgical matters more than speed)
